sections.title: ShEPhERD-score: Fast, adaptable three-dimensional alignment of molecular features
sections.abstract: ShEPhERD-score unifies differentiable 3D molecular similarity scoring and alignment, with CPU/GPU kernels for virtual screening and pairwise workflows.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report comparable-or-better performance than corresponding open-source tools in 8 of 9 DUDE-Z comparisons, up to 46-fold speedups, and target-dependent best scoring modes.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a software and virtual-screening benchmark, not experimental hit-rate or therapeutic evidence; the paper notes no one scoring representation is best for every target and suggests target-specific calibration.

sections.title: Dynamical Variational Theory of Stochastic Reaction Networks
sections.abstract: A field-theoretic variational approximation estimates stochastic reaction-network means, correlations, responses, and steady states in low-copy-number systems.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report numerical tests on gene regulation, enzyme kinetics, and infection dynamics, where their generalized self-consistent bubble resummation captures time-varying behavior and fluctuations missed by selected approximations.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a mathematical and numerical method, not a new wet-lab study. Its accuracy depends on the tested models and comparisons; the authors describe further numerical-solver work as an open direction.

sections.title: Ab-initio cryo-EM reconstruction from moments of denoised images
sections.abstract: The authors estimate an initial 3D cryo-EM model from the first three moments of denoised particle images, avoiding explicit orientation estimation at this stage.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors show moment-based models can initialize high-resolution refinement on experimental datasets without assuming uniform particle orientations.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper reports lower-resolution initial models than VDAM or SGD; denoising biases the estimated moments and loses fine detail, and the authors describe the results as preliminary. Refinement can still reach comparable map quality in the reported tests.

sections.title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning for Shear Wave Speed Estimation in MR Elastography
sections.abstract: An end-to-end model combines undersampled MRI reconstruction with wave inversion to estimate tissue shear-wave-speed maps from measured k-space data.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 30% lower NRMSE than total-variation minimization and accurate shear-wave-speed estimation up to acceleration factor 19; the arXiv comment identifies an accepted IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering version (DOI: 10.1109/TBME.2026.3666306).
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation is on retrospectively highly undersampled brain MRE data plus in-vivo application; the abstract gives no sample size and does not establish clinical impact or prospective performance.

sections.title: Geometry-bridge flow matching for blind rigid-motion correction in head cone-beam CT
sections.abstract: A geometry-bridge flow-matching prior jointly supports rigid-motion correction and pose estimation in head cone-beam CT reconstruction.
sections.claimed_contribution: On simulated 360-view scans from 30 held-out CQ500 patients, the authors report mean PSNR 37.1 dB and detector-plane reprojection error 0.27 mm; against image-linear training, the geometry bridge improved PSNR by 1.6 dB and reduced reprojection error by 33%.
sections.unique_caveat: The tests use simulated scans, a 30-patient held-out cohort, and nominal motion bounded at 10 mm / 10 degrees. This is not prospective clinical validation or evidence of improved patient outcomes.

sections.title: An Explainable and Scalable Hierarchical Tensor Framework for Integrating Multi-Omics and Digital Pathomics
sections.abstract: HIT-Fuse integrates six molecular and pathology modalities across four TCGA cancer cohorts, reconstructing missing latent modalities and providing tensor-based attributions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report survival-stratified subgroups and cohort-specific prediction gains, including a 56.4% relative weighted-F1 increase for glioma in their cohort-expansion experiment, with biological checks against DepMap, miRTarBase, and RPPA annotations.
sections.unique_caveat: The analyses use TCGA cohorts and reconstructed missing modalities; survival stratification and feature annotations do not establish prospective prognostic value or causal biology, and the reported gain is cohort-specific.

sections.title: From Sequence Uncertainty to Phenotype Hypotheses: Uncertainty-Conditioned Inference over Biomedical Knowledge Graphs
sections.abstract: An uncertainty-conditioned path-energy method converts genomic-model outputs into distributions over graph-supported gene-disease-phenotype hypotheses without patient-level phenotype supervision.
sections.claimed_contribution: On AlzKB and Hetionet, the authors report phenotype-entropy correlations with upstream uncertainty and held-out graph-recovery results; under gene hold-out, recall@10 exceeded DistMult on 24 of 30 masks, with the difference mainly attributable to three genes with many variants.
sections.unique_caveat: This evaluates graph-supported hypotheses, not patient diagnosis or validated phenotype prediction; the authors explicitly limit the gene-held-out result and note the concentration of gains in a few genes.

sections.title: When Foundation Models Disagree: Representational Heterogeneity for Calibrated Uncertainty in Whole-Slide Image Classification
sections.abstract: CALIFUSE uses disagreement among pathology foundation-model representations and chunk-level evidence consistency to estimate confidence in whole-slide classifications.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report better calibration, misclassification detection, and selective prediction than a strongest single-encoder baseline and naive ensemble averaging while maintaining competitive balanced accuracy.
sections.unique_caveat: These are task-benchmark results; the abstract does not give cohort sizes or establish performance in clinical workflows or across new institutions.

sections.title: GraphEP: A Calibrated Data System and Benchmark for Learning Cardiac Electrophysiology
sections.abstract: GraphEP packages graph-native cardiac electrophysiology simulations and benchmarks neural models for predicting transmembrane-potential trajectories.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that physiological model structure gives the strongest inductive bias in their benchmark, with HGT-Lag and GAP2ODE leading on complementary prediction metrics.
sections.unique_caveat: The benchmark consists of simulations, not experimentally measured or clinical cardiac trajectories; performance on real-world recordings remains to be established.

sections.title: Transition Dynamics Matter: Hidden Markov Scoring of Epileptogenic Channels in SEEG
sections.abstract: A joint hidden Markov model scores stereo-EEG channels by comparing latent-state transition probabilities between interictal periods and seizure onset.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved epileptogenic-zone localization versus a benchmark without latent-state structure, measured against medically validated zone definitions.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a retrospective algorithm evaluation in 30 patients, not a prospective test of surgical decisions or patient outcomes.

sections.title: Towards consensus on practical probabilistic evaluation metrics for clinical decision making in radiotherapy
sections.abstract: The authors assess probabilistic robustness metrics for proton radiotherapy using 60 plans from three Dutch centers and interviews with eight radiation oncologists.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that interviewed radiation oncologists considered the metrics suitable and mostly an improvement over their current robustness evaluation, while preferences differed by center and treatment site.
sections.unique_caveat: The study uses simulated treatments and interviews, not a prospective clinical-impact trial; the authors call for further consensus and clinical validation before broad implementation.

sections.title: The long-term divergence exponent and the temporal structure of step-to-step perturbations: a simulation study in two passive walking models
sections.abstract: Two passive-walker models test whether gait-stability divergence exponents respond to the temporal structure of step perturbations.
sections.claimed_contribution: In two passive models, the authors report that the long-term exponent increased with perturbation temporal correlation; the relation to perturbation amplitude differed between models, and human stride-series comparisons were descriptive.
sections.unique_caveat: Most evidence is simulation-based; the model-dependent response and descriptive human-series correlations do not establish clinical gait outcomes or a general mechanism.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.abstract: Molecular representations and reconstruction recur in ShEPhERD-score and the cryo-EM method, which address different computational tasks. HIT-Fuse, the phenotype-graph model, and CALIFUSE each handle heterogeneity or uncertainty in biomedical data, but do not validate one another. Reaction-network theory, GraphEP, and the passive-walker study model dynamics across distinct systems and evidence types. MRE, head cone-beam CT motion correction, SEEG localization, and radiotherapy robustness metrics are computational evaluations against biomedical measurements or definitions; none alone establishes prospective patient benefit.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.abstract: The papers motivate target- and scaffold-held-out biochemical assays for ShEPhERD-score and broader acquisition and denoising tests for cryo-EM; independent institutional validation for HIT-Fuse and CALIFUSE; patient-level blinded evaluation of genomic phenotype hypotheses; experimental electrophysiology validation for GraphEP; prospective multi-site MRE and SEEG evaluation; prospective head cone-beam CT tests; clinical decision-impact testing for radiotherapy metrics; and direct low-copy-number time series plus larger gait datasets for the reaction-network and passive-walker models.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.abstract: This batch offers methods for molecular screening, stochastic reaction dynamics, cryo-EM initialization, motion correction, and multimodal biomedical inference. The clearest attention signal is one current Semantic Scholar citation for the MRE paper, not a period gain or evidence of broad popularity. Experimental and prospective validation remains uneven across the corpus.
